study.title: Adaptive autonomous UAV scouting for rice lodging assessment using edge computing with deep learning EDANet
study.short_title: Adaptive autonomous UAV scouting for rice lodging assessment using edge computing with EDANet

segmentation.best_model: EDANet with RGB + ExG + ExGR input

dataset.name: Self-collected UAV RGB images of rice fields (Wufeng, Taiwan); two lodging events 2017 and 2019
dataset.note: Tables: 2017 collection 46,343x25,658 ortho at 200 m flight / 5.3 cm GSD; 2019 collection 5472x3648 at 50 m / 1.3 cm GSD and 200 m / 5.7 cm GSD. 215 50-m Wufeng images; 12 200-m images span the same area.

mIoU.ambiguity: mIoU not reported; paper uses precision/recall/accuracy/overall accuracy/F1.

F1.quote: Based on the results of the 2019 dataset, EDANet using RGB + ExG + ExGR information illustrations the highest value in recall (85.22%), accuracy (92.83%), and F1 score (78.51%).
F1.ambiguity: Macro F1-score on 2019 test dataset with the final RGB+ExG+ExGR model.

PA.quote: Based on the results of the 2019 dataset, EDANet using RGB + ExG + ExGR information illustrations the highest value in recall (85.22%), accuracy (92.83%), and F1 score (78.51%).
PA.ambiguity: Overall pixel accuracy (92.83%) on 2019 test dataset, final RGB+ExG+ExGR model.

crop_F1.ambiguity: Rice paddy class F1 95.28% (training, Table 5) is reported but not an RQ1 crop-F1 benchmark.

fps.ambiguity: Entire 2019 test process runs in ~1 minute (65 s) on a GPU workstation (Tesla V100), not per-image FPS or edge hardware.

latency_ms.ambiguity: Autonomous in-situ edge processing is simulated; Jetson TX2/AGX Xavier/Xavier NX listed as future work.

issues: 99.25% is scouting-normalization accuracy vs 50 m full scout, not segmentation accuracy; edge computing only simulated
